description:
FILED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05) with the measurement already taken, while
shipping #1181.

#1181 turned `@x = LIST` into ONE block copy.  For a FRESH producer's vector
(`sort`, `map`, `keys`, `split`, a range, a user-sub call — exactly
Pl/ClassicSort.pm's licence-B `_fresh_arg` classification) the copy is not
needed at all: the produced simple-vector could BE the array's storage.

THE MEASUREMENT (scratch/s470bn/ab-lisp.pl, listcopy shape, 50 elements x 1 M):
  today (before #1181)                    0.51 s
  #1181's block copy (portable `replace`) 0.128 s
  zero-copy via sb-kernel:set-array-header 0.089 s   ** -30 % of what is left **
So the residue is small beside #1181's own -72 %, which is why it was not taken.

WHAT IT NEEDS: (a) `sb-kernel:set-array-header array data length fill-pointer
0 (list length) nil nil` — SBCL's own adjust-array primitive, one more internal
beside %p-vec-data's `sb-kernel:%array-data`; (b) a compile-time FRESHNESS fact
reaching `p-array-=` (the emitter knows it; ClassicSort's `_fresh_arg` is the
predicate, and rule 11 says move it to a shared home rather than copy it).

BAR: the seventeen probe shapes in Pl/t/perf-levers-01.t, plus the aliasing one
adoption could break that a copy cannot — a producer whose vector something
else still holds.


=== SIZED s473p (2026-09-07), and the GROWTH half SHIPPED without the fact ===

TWO FINDINGS, and the first one retargets this task.

(1) THE ROW THIS TASK WAS SIZED AGAINST CANNOT TAKE ADOPTION.  `listcopy` is
`my @c = @src` in a loop, and `@src` is an EXISTING array whose values perl
COPIES — adoption needs a FRESH producer (`sort`, `map`, `keys`, `split`, a
sub call), which `@c = @src` is not.  The task's own 0.128 -> 0.089 s
measurement is therefore of a shape `listcopy` does not have.  The qualifying
shapes have no bench row at all, and the range case (`@a = (1..$n)`) already
has #1204's path, which never materialises a vector.  **So #1182 needs a bench
row for `my @c = sort/map/keys/split(...)` BEFORE it is taken.**

(2) THE WIN IS IN THE GROWTH, NOT THE COPY, AND IT NEEDS NO FACT.  Measured
three ways on one core, best-of-5, a fresh `my @c` filled from a source vector
(scratch/s473p/probe5.lisp + probe6.lisp in the s473p worktree):

    elements   ADJUST-ARRAY + replace   fresh header + replace   full adoption
           5          110 ms                    50 ms                42 ms
          50           15 ms                     9 ms                 8 ms
        2000            4 ms                     4 ms                 5 ms

`adjust-array`'s job is to PRESERVE the old contents, and a whole-array
assignment has already set the fill pointer to 0 and is about to write every
slot — so it is preserving a buffer nobody will read.  Installing a FRESH
element vector through `sb-kernel:set-array-header` instead gets essentially
all of adoption's win, keeps perl's value-copy semantics, and requires no
freshness fact of any kind.  At 2 000 elements the copy dominates and full
adoption is actually SLOWER than the fresh header, so the fact would buy
nothing at the top end either.

SHIPPED as `%p-array-grow-discarding` (commit `39e1a656`, s473p), called from the two `p-array-fill`
sites whose contents are discarded (the bulk-fill growth and the slow path's
#981 reserve).  The RANGE fill's `adjust-array` (p-.. into a place at a
non-zero fill pointer) is NOT changed: that one APPENDS, so its old contents
are live.  Header fields probed field by field against `adjust-array`'s
result: array-dimension, array-total-size, the fill pointer,
adjustable-array-p, array-header-p, array-displacement, %p-vec-data's answer,
EQUALP after the fill, and growth by vector-push-extend / %p-vpush afterwards.
Declines to `adjust-array` for a displaced array or anything that is not the
plain element-storage shape (`%p-vec-data`'s own definition), and does nothing
for a non-adjustable one, which is what the callers' guard did.
SBCL-specific like `%p-vec-data`'s own `sb-kernel:%array-data` beside it;
VERIFIED ON SBCL 2.6.0.debian (the 2.5.2 floor is not on this machine — a
future session on 2.5.2 should re-verify the symbol and the arglist).

MEASURED as a runtime A/B (`BENCH_RT_B` against the previous runtime,
interleaved, BENCH_K=5, two rounds; B/A > 0 means the OLD runtime is slower):
    listcopy   +28.7 %   +27.0 %      (0.2694 -> 0.2093 s, 0.43x -> 0.33x)
    slices     +19.9 %   +20.9 %
    controls:  cfor +0.9/+7.2, arrhash +1.6, arrfill +2.9/-2.3, sortnum +2.6,
               sliceasgn -1.6, pushloc -0.7, feread2 +0.4, feread3 -0.1,
               arrhash-k -3.4, feread -7.0  (all noise; the box was shared)


STATUS after s473p: this task stays OPEN for the ADOPTION half, and it now
names its own precondition -- a bench row for `my @c = sort/map/keys/split(...)`,
since `listcopy` cannot exercise adoption at all.  The growth half shipped in
`39e1a656` and is NOT what this task asks for.
subject: true storage ADOPTION for a FRESH producer vector: a further -30 % of what #1181 leaves (measured), via an SBCL array-header install + a compile-time freshness fact
